title: Synapse analysis declaration
description: THE DEMAND SIDE. What a consumer NEEDS, as data. The capability and signal contracts describe what Synapse OFFERS; nothing described what anything REQUIRED, so an analysis's inputs could only be discovered by running it. EXTRACTED from writing dead_stock, not designed in advance: every field here exists because that declaration could not be written without it. ON THE TWO FIELDS THIS DESCRIPTION USED TO CALL ABSENT: a SCHEDULE is still not here and deliberately never will be — cadence is a per-tenant SELECTION and lives in synapse.provision, because when a customer is analysed is an operational fact that changes without a release. An OUTPUT DESTINATION is still absent for the original reason, that nothing delivers anything. What did arrive is `max_rung`, which is the ENVELOPE rather than either of those: how far an action from this analysis is PERMITTED to travel, for any tenant. It is here and not in the table because it is a property of the analysis's maturity, and raising it should be a reviewed diff.

version.description: SemVer, matching the capability contract's discipline. A rule whose threshold or inputs change is a different rule, and a consumer must be able to pin which one it ran.

grain.description: The columns that together identify ONE emitted row. MUST BE CONTAINED IN EVERY REQUIRED CAPABILITY'S GRAIN, checked at registry import — an analysis emitting one row per (tenant, store, sku) can only join capabilities that identify rows at least that finely, and a coarser capability cannot be joined without inventing rows. This is the first mechanical use of the capability contract's `grain`, and the reason that field was worth extracting from one resolver.

requires.description: The capabilities this analysis reads, with the fields it reads from each and the gates it binds on each. NON-EMPTY: an analysis with no inputs has nothing to analyse.

capability_id.description: Must name a REGISTERED capability. A requirement on an unregistered one is a declaration that can never resolve; a requirement on a DECLINED one fails at import with the recorded reason attached.

fields.description: The subset of that capability's `returns` this analysis reads. Checked against `returns` at import, which is what would catch reaching for a plausible-but-absent field — the most likely way an analysis goes quietly wrong. NON-EMPTY: an analysis that reads nothing from a capability does not require it.

gates.description: Thresholds this analysis binds on that capability's declared gate KINDS, each with the policy for reducing a per-series measurement to a verdict. THIS IS THE FIELD THE CAPABILITY CONTRACT GAVE UP: it held `min_history_days: 60` on the supply side, which works for one caller and breaks for two — dead stock wants 90 days of no-sales, a forecast wants 60 for seasonality, and both read the same rows. An EMPTY ARRAY is a claim that the capability declares no gates, and the binding must match its declared kinds exactly: an unbound declared gate never runs, and a bound undeclared gate has no probe.

days.description: Minimum DISTINCT dates carrying data, per series — coverage, not calendar span. A forecaster needs observations, not distance. Minimum 1: zero is not a requirement, it is the absence of one, and the empty array says that.

policy.description: What 'enough' MEANS across a population of series. all_series = every series must clear the threshold ('forecast every SKU'); any_series = one qualifying series is enough ('forecast anything', and what a console asking 'is this usable here at all' means). Both are legitimate and neither is derivable from data, which is why a caller must state it and why slice 1's unowned default was deleted rather than tuned. MIN-over-series is deliberately not a value: it is all_series with a worse name, and it reads as conservative while being unusable on any growing catalogue.

window_from_threshold.description: The DATE WINDOW this requirement needs, named as one of the declaration's own thresholds. The operational half of the capability contract's `freshness`: AS_OF_DATE has said since slice 1 which capabilities a date parameter is meaningful for, and this is what it costs to call one. Resolved against the caller's `as_of` (date_from = as_of - (days - 1)), because a window is relative to the moment of asking and cannot be a literal here. Declaring one against a LAST_WRITE capability is a contradiction the registry refuses at import. Absent for a capability that takes no window.

emits.description: The field names this analysis PRODUCES. Declared before anything consumed them, and the payoff arrived: the evaluator's row type is checked against this at registry import, and the action proposer reads these findings by name. A scorer, when it exists, is checkable against this too.

thresholds.description: Numbers the ANALYSIS ITSELF uses, as distinct from gates on a capability. A gate decides whether a capability may be READ; a threshold is arithmetic over rows already fetched. dead_stock's stale_after_days is the second kind: no read depends on it, and it is the whole content of the rule.

fitted.description: TRUE when the number is derived from the tenant's own data. FALSE when it is a constant, in which case `stands_in_for` is REQUIRED — a number with no stated derivation is indistinguishable from a number someone guessed, and the standing rule is that thresholds are fitted where possible and honest about it where not.

stands_in_for.description: What a CONSTANT threshold substitutes for, and ideally how the fitted version would be computed. Required when fitted is false, forbidden when it is true (a fitted threshold stands in for nothing).

holdout.description: THE EXPERIMENT DESIGN, or null when the analysis produces no actions. NOT OPTIONAL AND NOT DEFAULTED: null is a claim that nothing is acted on, and a missing key is a silence. An analysis with an action proposer MUST have one, checked at registry import, because an action without an arm cannot be analysed and a counterfactual cannot be built retrospectively — assignment has to exist from the first action ever recorded. Declared here rather than supplied per call, unlike a gate threshold: changing the unit, the fraction or the salt INVALIDATES the comparison, so it belongs on the versioned thing.

unit.description: The assignment grain, a subset of the analysis grain (checked at import). Per-SKU for dead_stock: per-STORE is the cleaner comparison in general and unusable for a two-store tenant, where two units cannot be randomised and any difference measured is a store difference.

holdout_percent.description: Percent of subjects held back. 1..99: 0 is not a holdout and 100 treats nobody, and neither is an experiment.

salt.description: Fixed input to the assignment hash, so the same subject lands in the same arm on every run without anything being stored. EXPLICIT rather than derived from id+version, so a version bump chooses whether to reshuffle.

fitted.description: TRUE when the fraction comes from a power calculation. FALSE requires stands_in_for — same one-way rule as a threshold.

max_rung.description: THE ENVELOPE: the furthest a produced action may travel, for ANY tenant. A provision binds a rung; a provision naming a rung above this is refused when it is LOADED, so an over-privileged provision never reaches an orchestrator. `shadow` means compute, record, show nobody — the only rung anything implements. `suggest` means an action reaches a human and NOTHING IMPLEMENTS IT; it is named so the envelope check is testable rather than vacuous, and so that enabling delivery is the deletion of an explicit refusal rather than the addition of an enum member.
